name: Grand Island
blurb: The Night of the Twisters. Seven tornadoes over one small city in three hours, three of them turning anticyclonically — backwards — which almost nothing does.
source: NOAA Storm Prediction Center tornado database (1950–2025)
pathFidelity: all seven tornadoes digitised from Fujita & Wakimoto's damage map: the centrelines as drawn, the F1–F4 isopleths, and Fujita's clock times

torn.name: Grand Island No. 1 (cyclonic), NE
torn.timing: Fujita's clock times along the path
sources: Fujita & Wakimoto (1982), Anticyclonic tornadoes in 1980 and 1981 — damage map (inset)
torn.story: Touched down north of Prairie Creek, eleven miles north-west of the city, and wandered south-east for fifty minutes in loops — seven miles on the ground as the crow flies, fourteen and a half as it actually went — into the Capital Heights subdivision on the north-west edge of town. A woman driving to a relative's farm was killed.

torn.name: Grand Island No. 2 (anticyclonic), NE
torn.timing: Fujita's clock times along the path
sources: Fujita & Wakimoto (1982), Anticyclonic tornadoes in 1980 and 1981 — damage map (main map)
torn.story: A small anticyclonic tornado — turning clockwise, the wrong way — that dropped near Webb and Airport roads on the north-west side and lasted twelve minutes.

torn.name: Grand Island No. 3 (anticyclonic), NE
torn.timing: Fujita's clock times along the path
sources: Fujita & Wakimoto (1982), Anticyclonic tornadoes in 1980 and 1981 — damage map (main map)
torn.story: Also anticyclonic. It hooked south out of the fields between US-281 and Webb Road, then turned east-south-east across the north side of the city toward the Veterans hospital, F3 in places. One death, 40 injured.

torn.name: Grand Island No. 4 (anticyclonic), NE
torn.timing: Fujita's clock times along the path
sources: Fujita & Wakimoto (1982), Anticyclonic tornadoes in 1980 and 1981 — damage map (main map)
torn.story: The third anticyclonic tornado of the night: a short loop south-east of the city, curling from south-west to west to north.

torn.name: Grand Island No. 5 (cyclonic), NE
torn.timing: Fujita's clock times along the path
sources: Fujita & Wakimoto (1982), Anticyclonic tornadoes in 1980 and 1981 — damage map (main map)
torn.story: The killer. It came in from the east along Bismark Road at F3 to F4 — Fujita estimated winds of 250 mph in the worst of it — then turned hard south down South Locust Street, the city's business strip, and ground through it at a crawl: 1.1 miles on the record, six on the ground. Three people died in its path, 110 were injured, and the Locust Street corridor was flattened.

torn.name: Grand Island No. 6 (cyclonic), NE
torn.timing: Fujita's clock times along the path
sources: Fujita & Wakimoto (1982), Anticyclonic tornadoes in 1980 and 1981 — damage map (main map)
torn.story: Formed south-east of the city near Stuhr Road as tornado 5 was ending and swung in a broad counter-clockwise arc to the south and east — F2, 18 injured.

torn.name: Grand Island No. 7 (cyclonic), NE
torn.timing: Fujita's clock times along the path
sources: Fujita & Wakimoto (1982), Anticyclonic tornadoes in 1980 and 1981 — damage map (inset)
torn.story: The last of the seven, over open country south-east of the city toward Giltner: a mile-wide F1 that corkscrewed through loop after loop for three quarters of an hour, 13 miles of path to cover four.

story: On the night of 3 June 1980 a nearly stationary supercell sat over Grand Island, Nebraska, and for about three hours put down tornado after tornado on and around the city — seven in all, several of them after dark and wrapped in rain.

Ted Fujita and Roger Wakimoto's study of the night found that three of the seven turned anticyclonically — clockwise, against the rotation of almost every tornado in the northern hemisphere — which made Grand Island a case study for years.
Five people were killed and around two hundred injured, and the night became a children's novel and later a television film: Night of the Twisters.
